A1.justification: Both complete 11-page PDFs describe the same 3D-GSW research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original watermarking experiments on Blender, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360, including rendering quality, bit accuracy, attack robustness, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–3, ablations in Tables 4–5, and efficiency measurements in Table 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.6 retain the same frequency-guided densification, gradient mask, decoder procedure, and losses. Added explanatory wording does not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Blender, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360 coverage and the same watermark extraction scenarios under image and model distortions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain StegaNeRF+3D-GS, WateRF+3D-GS, and 3D-GSW without FGD. Table 6 also retains the original 3D-GS reference. No comparator is added or removed within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same 25 scenes, 32/48/64-bit messages, evaluation metrics, training settings, and image/model attack procedures. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component and subband ablations, gradient-mask comparison, Gaussian-removal sensitivity analysis, and robustness tests are retained. Tables 4–5 and Figures 5–8 contain the same analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five different seeds. Neither adds uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tabulated numbers and figure data are unchanged. Section 4.3 corrects the stated trend above 50% Gaussian removal: v2 says LPIPS decreases, while v3 says LPIPS performance decreases, consistent with the increasing LPIPS curve in Figure 8. This is a limited correction to result reporting.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their mathematical definitions remain unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about robust watermarking, rendering quality, FGD efficiency, gradient masking, wavelet-subband loss, and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and quality/capacity trade-offs remain the same. The revised approximately 28% removal summary restates the existing 28.13% finding. The decoder-pretraining limitation is retained, although it moves to page 9.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL to the abstract, providing a new resource-access pointer. Hardware, hyperparameters, and implementation instructions are unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish what resources the linked page provides.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 52 cited works and research positioning. Changes to reference back-pointers reflect pagination, without adding or removing literature.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose refinements, including clarifying high-frequency processing in the introduction, expanding the Section 3.5 heading, and revising the Gaussian-removal discussion. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same eight figures and six tables are retained. Table 4 moves within page 7, Table 5 moves to page 8, Figure 6 receives a caption edit, and surrounding text reflows. The displays are not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity by correcting the misleading LPIPS trend wording to agree with Figure 8, and improves resource discoverability through the project-page pointer. These are limited benefits; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
